title: Fleet headroom allocator and soft-quota playtest
content:
Summary:

This note captures the results from the week-long playtest of a lightweight headroom allocator plus a soft-quota admission policy intended to smooth GPU pressure during new model onboards. Goal: find a pragmatic, low-risk control that preserves tail latency SLOs while minimizing cold-start KV eviction storms and allowing modest onboarding velocity. This is not the final design — it’s a test log + recommended param ranges for Q2 rollouts.

Key idea (one-liner):
- Reserve a small, region-aware cushion of GPU slots (headroom) and limit model admission with a soft quota that temporarily rejects or shifts lower-priority traffic when cache pressure or slot saturation approaches thresholds. Soft rejections are accompanied by pre-warmed fallback model routing.

Why we ran this playtest:
- Observed repeated KV cache churn and eviction waves when 2+ large open models were admitted to a region in <48h.
- Existing hard quotas are effective but slow (manual capacity adds) and frustrate product teams.
- We need a strategy that keeps production latency stable during moderate onboarding bursts and lets growth teams move faster while we provision capacity.

Assumptions used for simulations and testbed:
- Test region = us-west2 (Nvidia H100, 8-GPU clusters).
- Baseline fleet utilization before new onboarding: 68% average, 78% 95th percentile.
- Typical long-form chat P50 = 90ms token latency, P95 = 300ms; target SLO: P95 < 350ms.
- New model profile: 70B dense model, KV working set ~1.8GB per concurrent session average, typical prefix reuse 25% for seeded traffic.
- Admission window modeled over 72 hours with staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Headroom allocator design (prototype):
- Compute per-region target headroom H_r = max(5% of cluster slots, 8 GPU-equivalent slots) + dynamic component tied to KV eviction rate.
- Headroom maintained by marking slots as "standby" (no new admittances) and allowing ephemeral warmup traffic (internal warmers only).
- If region-wide available slots <= H_r and a new admission request arrives, the soft-quota path triggers.

Soft-quota behavior (prototype rules):
- Soft limit L_r = floor( total_model_slots_r * (1 - headroom_fraction) ). Admission above L_r is allowed only if:
  - request priority is high (system/internal), OR
  - KV eviction rate < 0.6 evictions/min per host AND GPU usage < 88%.
- Otherwise: instead of hard rejecting, the request is routed to:
  1) Pre-warmed smaller variant (quantized) if available; OR
  2) Lower-latency cached variant; OR
  3) Queue for up-to 6s for slot to free, then retry with exponential backoff.

Playtest topology and workloads:
- Two test clusters in us-west2: cluster-A (primary serving), cluster-B (spillover candidate).
- Workload generator ran a mix of 60% production-recorded traces + 40% synthetic long-form sessions to stress KV.
- Admission events: 3 staged model admits from 2026-02-03 to 2026-02-06; each admit replaced 8 GPUs worth of demand (simulating multiple tenants onboarding).

Observations & metrics (high level):
- Latency: P95 token latency increased by median +18ms during admits with headroom+soft-quota vs +72ms without controls.
- KV evictions: Eviction spike amplitude reduced by ~62% when headroom was active; time to steady-state eviction rate shortened from ~14h to ~6h.
- GPU utilization: Peak utilization still reached 94% in uncontrolled runs. With allocator active, peak stayed near 89% (within safety band).
- Admission behavior: ~14% of admission attempts went to fallback quantized variant; 6% were queued briefly; hard rejects were ~0.7% (mostly low-priority background batch jobs).

Behavioral notes (qualitative):
- Pre-warmed fallback variants improved perceived quality for many prompts, but not all (edge-case hallucinations slightly more frequent). Need to couple with quality monitoring to spot regressions.
- Queueing for 0–6s was acceptable for low-priority clients; high-priority interactive sessions required immediate fallback routing.
- Keeping a region-local pool of standby slots made rolling restarts and maintenance less disruptive.

Parameter sensitivity (playtest sweep):
- Headroom fraction sweep: 3% / 5% / 8% / 12%
  - 3%: insufficient to curb eviction storms on multi-model admits.
  - 5%: reasonable tradeoff; reduced most eviction spikes with ~1.5% lost throughput capacity.
  - 8%: very stable but reduced available headroom for short-term bursts to onboard; slightly higher cost.
  - 12%: heavy safety cushion — high cost, good stability; recommended only for critical-regions during major launches.

- Eviction-rate threshold for soft acceptance: 0.4–0.7 evictions/min per host looked good. Lower threshold is conservative and causes more fallbacks (lowered QPS).

Operational playbook (recommended):
- Default headroom fraction per region: 5% (min 8 gpu-equivalent slots).
- For flagged launches (>=2 large models onboarding in 48h): temporarily bump to 8% and enable more aggressive warmers.
- Soft-quota enforcement: start in "observe-only" for the first real-customer rollout, then flip to active after 2 successful soft rollouts.
- Fallback routing: require a validated quantized variant for each catalog model before soft-quota active. If none, route to queued retry with smart backoff.

Dashboards & alerts to add:
- Regional headroom fill ratio (standby slots / H_r) — alert if > 85% consistently for > 10m.
- KV eviction rate per host (1m, 5m, 1h windows) and 95th-percentile client latency correlated to eviction spikes.
- Admission fallback rate and quality regressions tied to fallback variants (alert if fallback_quality_drop > 2% over baseline).

Gaps & follow-ups:
- Need end-to-end eval harness to synthesize realistic fallback quality regressions (automated prompt sets + eval metrics).
- Explore combining soft-quota with temporary regional scaling (fast-provision lightweight GPU pools for warmers) — early cost estimate attached in linked artifact.
- Investigate client-side backoff SDK patterns so product teams can opt-in to low-latency fallback vs queueing behavior.

Recommendations for Q2 rollout (incremental plan):
1) Ship headroom allocator as a toggle behind a config flag in us-west2 test clusters. Run in observe-only for 2 weeks.
2) Require fallback variant artifacts to be checked into model catalog whenever teams request admission.
3) After two successful observe cycles, enable soft-quota enforcement for tenant onboarding paths that have agreed SLA/priority labels.
4) Maintain default headroom = 5% but allow automated bump to 8% when onboarding events exceed defined velocity thresholds.

Appendix: quick numbers used in playtest (human-readable):
- Typical slot = 1 GPU-equivalent (H100).
- Cluster size = 128 GPU-equivalent slots.
- Headroom 5% => 6 slots. 8% => 10 slots.
- New model admission increment per stage = 8 slots equivalent.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- How do we compensate teams for fallback-induced quality deltas? Consider SLA credits, or a pre-launch sandbox test requirement.
- Are there regulatory regions where we must avoid cross-region fallbacks? Flag APAC customers.
- Can release-engineering provide a lightweight automated quantization path that lives in PR pipelines?

If folks want the raw test logs and plots (eviction over time, per-host latency series), see the linked GitHub PR where the artifacts are uploaded (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/512).

End.
